title: Braised Short Ribs
description: Beef short ribs simmered low and slow with radish, carrot and chestnuts in a sweet soy braise until the meat falls off the bone.

ingredients.item: Korean radish, peeled and cut into chunks

ingredients.note: or use canned/jarred if fresh are unavailable

steps: Soak the short ribs in cold water for 1 hour, changing the water once, to draw out excess blood.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the ribs and blanch for 5 minutes; drain and rinse off the scum.
Whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, grated pear, garlic, ginger and sesame oil together in a bowl to make the braising sauce.
Return the ribs to a clean pot, pour in the sauce plus 2 cups water, cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 40 minutes.
Add the radish and carrot chunks and continue simmering, covered, for 30 minutes until the meat is fork-tender.
Add the chestnuts and simmer uncovered for a final 15 minutes, spooning sauce over the ribs, until it thickens and coats everything glossy.
Stir in the scallions during the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Transfer to a serving platter and scatter with toasted sesame seeds before serving.
tips: Blanching the ribs first is what keeps the braise clean-tasting instead of murky; don't skip it.
The dish tastes even better the next day once the sauce has fully penetrated the meat — make it a day ahead for gatherings.
kidNote: Not spicy at all; shred a rib off the bone for younger kids and spoon extra sauce over rice.
nutritionNote: Rich in protein and iron from the beef; the braise is sodium-heavy from soy sauce, so balance the plate with plain rice and a raw vegetable side rather than more banchan.

title: Boiled Pork Wraps
description: Pork belly simmered whole in aromatics until silky, then sliced thin and wrapped in lettuce with garlic, ssamjang and fresh kimchi.

ingredients.note: tenderizes and deodorizes the pork; optional but recommended

ingredients.item: head butter or romaine lettuce, leaves separated
fresh radish salad or mild kimchi

steps: Fill a large pot with enough water to cover the pork, then whisk in the doenjang until dissolved.
Add the onion, smashed garlic, ginger and coffee granules, then bring to a boil over high heat.
Lower the pork belly in, reduce to a simmer, cover and cook for 50 to 60 minutes until a chopstick slides through easily.
Lift the pork out and rest it for 10 minutes so the slices hold together when cut.
Slice the pork against the grain into pieces about 5mm thick.
Arrange the sliced pork on a platter with the lettuce leaves, sliced garlic, ssamjang and radish salad or kimchi.
Let everyone build their own wrap: a lettuce leaf topped with pork, a dab of ssamjang, a garlic slice and a bit of radish salad.
tips: Simmer gently rather than at a rolling boil, or the pork toughens instead of turning silky.
Slice only what you'll serve right away; the rest keeps better as one piece, chilled, and reheated in the broth.
kidNote: Serve the kids their pork plain in lettuce with just a rice-vinegar dab instead of ssamjang, which has some heat from gochujang.
nutritionNote: A fattier cut balanced by lettuce and radish; keep the ssamjang portion small since it is concentrated in salt from doenjang and gochujang.

title: Grilled Pork Belly with Ssamjang
description: Thick-cut pork belly grilled at the table until crisp-edged, then wrapped in lettuce with garlic, ssamjang and a squeeze of sesame oil.

ingredients.item: head lettuce or perilla leaves, separated
toasted sesame oil, with a pinch of salt
onion, thinly sliced, tossed with a little soy sauce and sesame oil

steps: Heat a heavy skillet or tabletop grill over medium-high heat with no oil; the pork belly renders its own fat.
Lay the pork belly slices in a single layer and let them sear undisturbed for 2 to 3 minutes until golden underneath.
Flip and cook the other side for 2 minutes, then use kitchen scissors to snip the strips into bite-sized pieces.
Push the pork to the side, add the sliced garlic and kimchi if using, and let them sizzle in the rendered fat for 1 to 2 minutes.
Continue cooking the pork pieces, turning occasionally, until deeply golden and crisp at the edges, about 8 to 10 minutes total.
Wipe away excess oil pooling in the pan with a paper towel as needed so the meat crisps rather than stews.
Serve straight from the pan with lettuce, ssamjang, sesame oil dip and the onion salad for wrapping.
tips: Resist flipping constantly — one good sear per side gives the best crust.
Snipping with scissors instead of a knife is the traditional (and easiest) way to portion it tableside.
kidNote: Plain grilled pork belly is naturally mild; skip the green chili and ssamjang for the kids and give them a dot of sesame oil and salt instead.
nutritionNote: High in fat from the pork belly; balance the meal with the lettuce wraps and onion salad for volume and fibre rather than extra rice.

title: Spicy Stir-Fried Chicken
description: Boneless chicken thigh stir-fried with cabbage, sweet potato and rice cakes in a fiery gochujang glaze, Chuncheon-style.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thigh, cut into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.note: soaked if hard, or use frozen

steps: Whisk the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, rice wine, garlic and ginger together to make the sauce.
Toss the chicken pieces with half the sauce and let marinate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Heat the oil in a wide, flat pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the marinated chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes until it starts to brown at the edges.
Add the sweet potato and remaining sauce, cover, and cook for 5 minutes until the sweet potato starts to soften.
Add the cabbage and rice cakes, stir to coat, and cook uncovered for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and the cabbage wilts.
Stir in the scallions during the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Serve straight from the pan; stir any leftover rice into the pan drippings at the end for a bonus fried rice.
tips: Use a wide shallow pan rather than a deep pot so everything sears instead of steams.
If the pan looks dry as it cooks, add a splash of water rather than more oil.
kidNote: This one is properly spicy and not a kid dish as written; set aside plain-grilled chicken pieces before saucing, or make a mild soy-garlic version with the same vegetables for the kids.
nutritionNote: The gochujang-based sauce is high in sodium; the cabbage and sweet potato add fibre, so serve with extra plain rice and water rather than more sauce.

title: Spicy Beef and Vegetable Soup
description: Shredded brisket simmered with fernbrake, bean sprouts and scallion in a smoky red broth, the soup Koreans reach for on a cold day.

ingredients.note: or substitute extra bean sprouts if unavailable

steps: Place the brisket in a pot, cover with 2.5 liters of water and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce to a simmer and cook, covered, for 50 minutes until the beef is tender; remove the beef and reserve the broth.
Once cool enough to handle, shred the beef into bite-sized strips by hand along the grain.
In a small bowl, mix the gochugaru with the oil to make a chili oil paste; this keeps the color vivid instead of dull.
Heat a large pot over medium heat, add the chili oil paste, garlic, soy sauce and fish sauce, and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the shredded beef and fernbrake and stir-fry for 2 minutes to coat in the seasoning.
Pour in the reserved broth, bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the bean sprouts and scallions, simmer for a final 5 minutes, and season with salt to taste before serving hot.
tips: Toasting the gochugaru in oil before it hits the broth is what gives the soup its signature red color and depth, not just heat.
Shred the beef by hand rather than slicing — it holds the sauce better and is the traditional texture.
kidNote: This soup is genuinely spicy; ladle out plain broth and shredded beef for the kids before the chili oil paste goes in, and season their portion separately with just soy sauce.
nutritionNote: A good source of iron and protein from the brisket; the broth is salty from soy and fish sauce, so serve with plain rice rather than extra banchan.

title: Beef Short Rib Soup
description: A clean, clear broth of long-simmered short ribs and radish, seasoned simply with salt, garlic and scallion — the soup Koreans serve on special occasions.

ingredients.item: Korean radish, cut into large chunks

steps: Soak the short ribs in cold water for 1 hour, changing the water once, to draw out blood.
Bring a pot of water to a boil, blanch the ribs for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse each piece clean.
Return the ribs to a clean pot with 3 liters of fresh water, the onion, garlic and ginger.
Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer, skimming occasionally, and cook covered for 1 hour.
Add the radish chunks and continue simmering for another 40 minutes until both meat and radish are tender.
Remove the onion and ginger, then slice the radish into smaller bite-sized pieces if large.
If using, add the soaked glass noodles and simmer for 5 minutes until translucent.
Season the broth with salt and black pepper to taste, ladle into bowls and top with sliced scallion.
tips: A long, gentle simmer rather than a hard boil keeps the broth clear instead of cloudy.
This soup freezes well without the noodles — add fresh noodles only when reheating to serve.
kidNote: Naturally mild and kid-friendly; just check for small bone fragments before serving to the 6-year-old.
nutritionNote: A light, protein-rich broth lower in sodium than most Korean soups since it is seasoned mainly with salt; a good one to serve more often.

title: Braised Mackerel with Radish
description: Mackerel fillets braised over sweet radish in a bubbling gochujang-gochugaru sauce until the fish is tender and the radish has soaked up all the flavor.

ingredients.item: whole mackerel, cleaned and cut into thick steaks
ingredients.note: ask the fishmonger to clean and cut it

steps: Whisk the gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce, rice wine, sugar, garlic and ginger with 1 cup water to make the braising sauce.
Line the bottom of a wide, shallow pot with the radish rounds and onion slices.
Lay the mackerel steaks skin-side up over the radish.
Pour the sauce evenly over the fish and vegetables and bring to a boil over high heat, uncovered.
Reduce to a medium simmer and cook for 15 minutes, occasionally spooning sauce over the fish.
Add the scallions, cover, and continue simmering for 10 minutes until the radish is fully tender and the sauce has thickened.
Scatter the red chili over the top for garnish just before serving.
Serve hot directly from the pot with steamed rice, spooning extra sauce and radish over each bowl.
tips: Don't stir once the fish is in — spoon sauce over it instead, or the steaks will break apart.
Buy the freshest mackerel you can find; the braise is simple enough that fish quality is what makes or breaks it.
kidNote: The chili-forward sauce is too spicy as written; flake off plain fish with a little of the softened radish before the dish finishes reducing, and rinse briefly if it caught too much sauce.
nutritionNote: Mackerel is rich in omega-3s, but the sauce is heavy in sodium from soy sauce and gochujang; balance with plain rice and a mild vegetable side.

title: Braised Tofu
description: Pan-fried tofu slices braised in a light soy-garlic sauce until they soak up all the savory glaze — a gentle, everyday banchan.
steps: Pat the tofu slices dry thoroughly with paper towels to help them crisp instead of splatter.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and fry the tofu slices for 3 minutes per side until lightly golden.
While the tofu fries, whisk the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, scallion and water together for the sauce.
Once both sides are golden, pour the sauce evenly over the tofu in the pan.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 8 minutes so the tofu absorbs the sauce.
Uncover and simmer for 2 more minutes, spooning sauce over the top, until it reduces to a light glaze.
Transfer to a serving plate and sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving warm.
tips: Drying the tofu well before frying is the difference between a crisp edge and a soggy one.
This keeps and reheats well, making it a good make-ahead banchan for the week.
kidNote: Naturally mild and a good kid side dish as written; no changes needed.
nutritionNote: A lean plant protein; the soy-based glaze adds sodium, so this pairs best with plain rice and a fresh vegetable rather than more salty banchan.

title: Spicy Radish Salad
description: Julienned Korean radish tossed with gochugaru, garlic and a touch of sugar and vinegar into a crunchy, tangy-sweet banchan eaten fresh, not fermented.

ingredients.note: use less for a milder salad
or substitute extra salt to keep it vegetarian

steps: Toss the julienned radish with the salt in a bowl and let it sit for 10 minutes to soften slightly.
Squeeze out any excess liquid the radish releases, but do not rinse it.
Add the gochugaru to the radish and toss well so every strand picks up color.
Add the rice vinegar, sugar, garlic, ginger and fish sauce, and mix thoroughly by hand.
Taste and adjust with more vinegar for tang or sugar for sweetness as needed.
Fold in the scallion and sesame seeds just before serving.
tips: Letting the radish sit with salt first keeps the salad crunchy instead of watery once dressed.
This is best eaten within a day or two, unlike fermented kimchi.
kidNote: Use the lower end of the gochugaru amount for the household batch, and set aside a portion before adding chili flakes, dressed with just vinegar and a little sugar, for the kids.
nutritionNote: Low-calorie and high in fibre from the radish; go light on the fish sauce and added salt since gochugaru alone brings plenty of flavor.

title: Spicy Cucumber Salad
description: Thinly sliced cucumber salted briefly for crunch, then tossed with garlic, gochugaru, vinegar and sesame into a bright, quick banchan.

ingredients.note: use less for a milder salad

steps: Toss the sliced cucumber with the salt and let sit for 10 minutes to release excess water.
Drain the cucumber and gently squeeze out any remaining liquid without crushing the slices.
In a bowl, mix the gochugaru, rice vinegar, sugar, garlic and sesame oil into a smooth dressing.
Add the cucumber to the dressing and toss well until every slice is coated.
Fold in the scallion and sesame seeds.
Serve immediately for the best crunch, or chill for 15 minutes if you prefer it cold.
tips: Salting and draining the cucumber first is what keeps the salad crisp instead of watery once dressed.
This dish is best made just before serving — it softens if it sits dressed for too long.
kidNote: Set aside a portion of salted cucumber before adding the gochugaru dressing, and toss the kids' share with just a little vinegar, sugar and sesame oil.
nutritionNote: Very low in calories and a good source of hydration and fibre; use a light hand with salt since the dressing already carries flavor from garlic and chili.
